description:
Bodikon (ボディコン), also referred to as Otachidai Gyaru (お立ち台ギャル), is a style and subculture centered around the distinctive style of dress of the same name, the bodycon (a shortening of the pronunciation of the English words "body conscious"). The style was not entirely based around the dress itself, however, and came to include the general female fashion of the Japanese Bubble Economy period.

Bodikon is the direct predecessor of Gyaru and all of its substyles. The first "Gals" were Bodikon women, and the emergence of the first Gyaru styles around 1993-1994 came largely from the "radicalisation" (described later on this page) of Bodikon style. Bodikon is therefore classified as "Gal," and can be considered part of the larger Ametora umbrella (which includes styles like Amekaji ), though it does not typically emulate 1980s and early 1990s American fashion trends.

This style was most popular in the mid-to-late 1980s and early 1990s, usually dated from late 1985 to 1994 at the peak of its popularity. It was influenced by the Japanese economy of the time, as well as the widespread popularity of dance-based nightlife in 1980s and 1990s Japan, especially venues playing Italo Disco , City Pop , Eurobeat, Hyper Techno/TechPara, and House music. There are also parallels with the mid-1980s Japanese trend of satirising and exaggerating American fashion and lifestyles.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Sexiness, strong confidence, fun, conspicuous consumption
